To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the translation process is a complex one, that the translator’s presence is felt throughout the TT and that a translation is a product of a series of choices made by the translator.
the TT is a product of the translator’s interpretation of the ST and that this interpretation is a function of the translator’s cultural and linguistic competence.

the translation of Hullabaloo in Guava Orchard by Kiran Desai is a successful translation, which is a good example of a translation that is not only a faithful representation of the source text, but which is also a work that can be read and enjoyed as a text in its own right.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the manner in which translation is a process of interpretation that can be described as a hermeneutic act.
the way the translator’s presence can be detected in her work, the extent to which it can influence the reader’s response and the way it can be measured.
the manner in which a TT is constructed, the translator’s role and the impact the TT has on the receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the translator’s choice of lexemes, the manner in which they are used in the context of the TT and the way the translator signals her own presence are of utmost importance for a good quality TT and for a successful translation process.
the TT, as a text, has been transformed and that it is the translator’s presence that has brought about this transformation.
the translator is a mediator between two cultures and that the translator’s presence can only be felt if the translation is evaluated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the translator’s choice of lexemes, the manner in which she uses them in the translation and the way in which she signals her presence in it, all have an impact on the receptor’s response.
the translator’s presence is a necessary evil that is unavoidable and that, if properly managed, it can lead to the creation of a new literary work.
the translator’s presence is not always a negative phenomenon, but rather one that can be used as a positive tool in the translation process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the translator is not a passive receiver but a conscious agent who is aware of her own role in the act of translation.
a translator must be a linguist and a cultural expert in order to achieve a good TT.
a translation is a text in itself and that it has its own value, independent of the ST.
